_provenance: Registry of economic models for the econ layer (design of 21.10.2026, docs/prereg_econ.md). Identities are arithmetic, tags are the analyst classification of each factor, thresholds are uncalibrated screens. No company data lives here; KPIs enter through facts.add_kpi with sources and available_at.

rules._status: uncalibrated screens chosen with nine analyst posts in view; frozen in docs/prereg_econ.md (21.10.2026); none may change after the held-out run (a bug is fixed, everything re-run, both results logged)

bases.balance: level at the period end (accounts, subscribers, client equity)
bases.average: average over the period (DARTs, average margin loans, MAPCs)
bases.flow: amount during the period (trips, net new accounts, bits shipped)
bases.cumulative: count since inception (products ever opened): never evidence of activity
bases.rate: a ratio or percentage (NDR, margin rate, a share)

structural.meaning: built over time and not lost in a bad year: accounts, customers, subscribers, bits

cyclical.meaning: rises and falls with the market, activity or the price cycle: trading, client equity, ASP, utilization

macro.meaning: set by rates, FX or policy, not by the company: margin rate, NIM, deposit cost advantage

mix.meaning: a change in composition: smaller new accounts, generation mix, top-N share; never reverted to a median

reclassification.meaning: an accounting or business-model change in what the line measures; only with evidence, then the unit basis is used

statuses.computed: value calculated, no reported line to check it against
statuses.consistent: within rules.identity_tolerance on levels, or within rules.growth_identity_pp on growth
statuses.partial: the identity explains less than rules.partial_below of the line; the residual is named
statuses.basis_mismatch: the inputs mix bases (constant currency vs reported); nothing is divided, both growth rates are shown, a question asks for the same-basis figure
statuses.scope_mismatch: the inputs differ in scope or window (US commercial vs total, TTM vs quarter, q/q vs y/y); nothing is computed
statuses.missing: an input is absent; the reading plan names it

identity_types.per_unit: line / units, annualized when the line is a quarter; end and average unit bases both shown when both exist
identity_types.product: product of the factors against the reported line; the gap is the residual (ln(1+g) = sum ln(1+g_i) + residual)
identity_types.share: part / total, and its share of incremental growth (d part / d total)

operating_expenses.note: OM = GM - opex/revenue exactly; the peak exception needs both

adjusted_ebitda.note: issuer definition stated; never mixed with operating income

commissions.note: pass-through fees (exchange, regulatory) stated and removed before growth is read

other_revenue.note: the line a thesis may rest on; thesis_on_minor_line reads its share of revenue and of incremental revenue

segment_profit.note: profit_definition stated (adjusted EBITDA, operating income, contribution)

deferred_revenue.note: a build is financing from customers (customer_prepayment_build)

receivables.note: growth compared with revenue growth over matched windows only

guarantee_maximum_exposure.note: a ceiling; never summed into a screen

deposit_funding_benefit.note: annual benefit of deposits versus alternative funding, when the issuer or an analyst states one

per_unit_vs_units.rule: units grow while the per-unit value falls more than rules.per_unit_fall

cyclical_deceleration.rule: across two reviews, cyclical factors slow by more than rules.cyclical_slowdown_pp while structural factors stay within +-rules.structural_stable_pp

rate_sensitivity_share.rule: annual impact of a 25bp move / annualized net interest income

take_rate_shift.rule: take rate (revenue / gross bookings) changes on a same-basis comparison; tagged reclassification only with evidence of a business-model change

expansion_led.rule: per-unit log share of growth above one half and NDR above rules.expansion_ndr_min

top_n_inconsistent.rule: the revenue implied by the top-N total (stated, or N x the top-N average) over the top-N share differs from a supplied revenue on the same scope and window (ttm_revenue for TTM) by more than rules.top_n_tolerance; never compared across scopes or windows

top_n_expansion.rule: top-N average growth (the set is re-ranked at each date: not same-customer growth), total (stated or N x average), revenue implied at the stated share, share trend (unknown without a prior share); compared only with revenue growth on the same scope and window, a split or line on another one is not_compared: scope_mismatch

thesis_on_minor_line.rule: the thesis line is below rules.minor_line_share of revenue; its share of incremental revenue is shown

core_units_flat.rule: core units move less than rules.flat_units_abs

disclosure_dropped.rule: a falsifier KPI stops being reported; the falsifier becomes unobservable

segment_unexplained.rule: a segment with at least rules.segment_material of revenue or profit has no reconciled identity

process_evidence.rule: renewed = a fall of at least rules.renewal_drawdown from a peak and a new high within rules.renewal_window_years (inclusive) on the stated years; machine working = at least one renewal, every known intensity flat (+-rules.intensity_flat_pp) or falling with R&D known, revenue CAGR >= rules.machine_growth_min; failing = an intensity rising >= rules.intensity_rising_pp while revenue growth slows; unproven otherwise; unknown when nothing could be read; a missing year is never interpolated; evidence to cite, never a moat rating

cash_conversion.rule: FCF / net income below rules.cfo_to_ni_min (no dedicated rule: the funding screen's CFO / NI threshold), net income positive, with the FCF basis labelled (cash block, else operating cash flow - capex from the lines)

peak_margin_run_rate.rule: owned by quarter._cycle: operating margin far above its own history; a quarter times four is peak earnings

operating_leverage_or_peak.rule: peak_margin_run_rate with leverage share -d(opex/revenue)/dOM >= rules.leverage_share_min, an evidenced model (econ.select's rule or an analyst override with evidence ids) that is not price-cyclical, and gross profit and opex present; both readings shown

margin_only_normalized.rule: run-rate earnings x evidenced cycle margin / current margin; a floor on the correction because revenue stays at the record run rate

lta_unproven.rule: contract coverage lacks one of: share of next-year volume, price floor or formula, deposits, tenor, or a source of the contracts block available at as_of is not an issuer document; no cycle damping

customer_concentration.rule: largest customers share of revenue and of receivables, from the concentration note

customer_prepayment_build.rule: deferred revenue builds (end above start): financing from customers, read with the funding ledger; when revenue growth exists over the same window the flag needs the build to grow faster than revenue, otherwise the comparison is not_computed: window_mismatch and the build is shown

ebitda_minus_capex.rule: segment EBITDA less segment capex, both on the issuer definition

cumulative_kpi_not_activity.rule: a cumulative KPI (products ever opened) is labelled cumulative and never read as activity

nco_basis.rule: loan sales are disclosed but only the headline NCO is supplied; a supplied normalized NCO is used and labelled

capital_lever_insufficient.rule: ROTE if all excess capital were returned (an upper bound) stays below the ROTE the price implies

excess_capital_range.rule: excess capital at both ends of an evidenced target range; never the midpoint

headroom_to_minimum.rule: capital ratio minus the regulatory minimum, in pp

funding_level.rule: high = firm exposure >= rules.firm_exposure_high and a statement check fails; elevated = one of the two; none otherwise; an analyst_estimate exposed share never sets it

cfo_to_ni.rule: CFO / NI and CFO / (NI - non-cash gains); below rules.cfo_to_ni_min fails; within rules.near_threshold prints with the threshold

receivables_vs_revenue.rule: receivables growth minus revenue growth over matched windows only; otherwise not_computed: window_mismatch

receivables_build_share.rule: receivables build (cash-flow statement, balance change shown beside it) as a share of net income

guarantee_ceiling.rule: contingent exposure "if called in full" against spendable cash; no probability; never summed into a screen

chain_exposure.rule: own share of revenue via the chain x upstream exposed share, only when both exist; otherwise unquantified with the missing numbers named

tranche_schedule_mismatch.rule: the period observed tranche, annualized, differs from the schedule by more than rules.tranche_mismatch; an open question

straight_line_assumed.rule: a schedule given only as a total and a number of years is straight-line and labelled an assumption

segment_reconciliation.rule: sum of segment revenue and profit against the consolidated lines, within rules.identity_tolerance

capex_per_unit_lag.rule: one quarter's capex over that quarter's capacity additions is refused: not_computed: construction lag

basis_mismatch.rule: constant currency against reported is never divided; both growth rates shown; a question asks for the same-basis figure

scope_mismatch.rule: scope or window differs; nothing is computed

mechanism.note: issuer documents only; analyst posts, consensus and assumptions do not answer these

kpis.connector_hint: AV/FMP structured data first, then the issuer release

marketplace.description: two-sided platform: revenue = gross bookings x take rate; gross bookings = consumers x frequency x bookings per trip

select.note: a gross_bookings/gmv KPI selects marketplace over the provider label (a ride-hailing company labelled Software - Application)

gross_bookings.note: gross value of transactions on the platform; not recognized revenue

gmv.note: gross merchandise value; same role as gross_bookings for goods marketplaces

mapcs.note: monthly active platform consumers, averaged over the quarter

trips.note: completed trips or orders in the period

frequency.note: trips per active consumer per period; derived when trips and mapcs are both reported

incentives.note: consumer incentives and supply spend; competitive, moves with rivalry

identities.note: growth check: ln(1+g_trips) against ln(1+g_mapcs) + ln(1+g_frequency)
same currency basis on both sides or basis_mismatch; tagged reclassification only with evidence of a business-model change, then falsifiers and margins move to the bookings basis
segment adjusted EBITDA per unit of that segment bookings (profit_definition stated)

find: business-model changes that move the revenue basis

questions: Is the take-rate change pricing, mix or a reclassification of what is booked as revenue?
Are more trips coming from more consumers or from more trips per consumer?

broker.description: revenue = accounts x revenue per account; revenue per account = equity per account (mix) x revenue yield on client equity (cyclical, macro)

select.note: financials + brokerage text + any of these KPIs: broker, not the loans/deposits tree

margin_rate.note: average rate earned on margin loans

rate_sensitivity_25bp.note: annual net-interest-income impact of a 25bp move, from 10-Q Item 3 or the release; per currency when given

identities.note: smaller new accounts lower it; never reverted
rates and activity; the only part of revenue per account that may revert
average balance x average rate against the reported line

questions: How much of the change in revenue per account is new-account mix, rates or activity?
How much net interest income moves per 25bp, and in which currencies?

data_platform_software.description: revenue = customers x revenue per customer; expansion (NDR) against new customers; top-N concentration

customers.note: paying customers; state the scope (US commercial vs total)

net_revenue_retention.note: trailing-twelve-month net dollar retention; expansion_led needs more than rules.expansion_ndr_min

arr.note: annual recurring revenue on the issuer definition

rpo.note: remaining performance obligations; current portion stated

top_n_average_revenue.note: average TTM revenue of the top N customers; N and window stated

top_n_share.note: top-N customers share of revenue on the same window

top_n_total_revenue.note: top-N customers revenue on the same window

identities.note: scope must match: US commercial revenue over US commercial customers
compared only with TTM revenue on the same window; never with a segment q/q split (scope_mismatch)

state: window: TTM vs quarter, q/q vs y/y

questions: How much of growth is new customers and how much is expansion of existing ones?
Is the top-N figure on the same scope and window as the growth being discussed?

consumer_innovator.description: revenue = sum of categories; the moat is a process: category renewal, new categories, innovation intensity

category_revenue.note: revenue by product category over several years; a renewal is a fall of at least rules.renewal_drawdown from the peak and a new high within rules.renewal_window_years

identities.note: the shares sum to one when every category is reported; a gap is named, never filled
printed as a change in pp, never "stable" by assumption

state: five fiscal years when available; a missing year is unknown, never interpolated

questions: Which categories fell from a peak and made a new high, and within how many years?
Did innovation intensity (R&D and advertising over revenue) stay flat while revenue grew?

memory_cycle.description: revenue = bits x ASP; margins swing with the price cycle; a record quarter is a run rate, not a base

bits.note: bits shipped; usually reported as a growth rate

asp.note: average selling price per bit; usually reported as a change

hbm_market_share.note: share of the high-bandwidth-memory market; a competitive position, stated with its source

state: bit growth and ASP change are usually growth rates, not levels

find: long-term agreements: tenor, deposits, price mechanism, share of next-year volume

questions: How much of revenue growth is bits and how much is ASP, and which part of ASP is HBM mix?
What share of next-year volume is covered by contracts with a price floor and deposits?

gpu_vendor.description: revenue = gigawatts shipped x revenue per gigawatt, by generation; the funding of the buyers is part of the read

gw_shipped.note: systems shipped measured in gigawatts; a capex-cycle volume

revenue_per_gw.note: revenue per gigawatt by product generation; the generation mix sets the average

questions: How many gigawatts shipped, at what revenue per gigawatt, by generation?
Who funds the customers' purchases: their own cash flow, debt, or the vendor's investments and guarantees?

compute_leasing.description: revenue = energized gigawatts x utilization x price per gigawatt-year; capex per gigawatt, tenor and customer credit decide the return

installed_capacity.note: energized capacity; capacity under construction earns nothing

contracted_backlog.note: take-or-pay and RPO; who the customers are

identities.note: one quarter's capex over that quarter's additions is refused: not_computed: construction lag

questions: What is the price per gigawatt-year, the contract tenor and the credit of the customers behind the backlog?
How much capacity is energized versus under construction, and who funds the build?

subscriber_network.description: revenue = average subscribers x ARPU; what is not subscriber x ARPU (hardware, enterprise, government) is named

arpu.note: monthly revenue per average subscriber (window: month); state whether hardware is included

paid_users.note: paid users of a subscription product; the same arithmetic as subscribers

identities.note: per period = average subscribers x monthly ARPU x months; end and average bases both shown; the residual is named and the identity stays partial

questions: How much of revenue is subscribers x ARPU, and what is the rest?
Is subscriber growth from new regions (structural) or from price (ARPU)?

digital_bank.description: net interest income = earning assets x NIM; products per member is cumulative; the capital lever is bounded

products.note: products ever opened; cumulative, never activity evidence

cross_buy_share.note: share of new products opened by existing members

deposit_cost_advantage.note: deposit cost below the alternative funding rate, in rate terms

nco_rate.note: headline net charge-off rate; with loan sales disclosed a normalized NCO must be supplied and labelled (nco_basis)

identities.note: annual benefit against alternative funding; compared with a supplied figure when one exists

questions: What ROTE does the price require, and can returning all excess capital reach it (an upper bound)?
Are charge-offs stated before or after delinquent-loan sales?

ads_platform.description: revenue = daily active users x ARPU, by geography; logged-in vs logged-out; licensing = contracts x renewal price

dau.note: daily active users; state logged-in vs total and the geography

arpu.note: revenue per average user in the period (window: the period); moves with ad pricing and demand

licensing_price.note: contract value at renewal; fixed-fee contracts move only at renewal

questions: Is growth coming from more users or from more revenue per user, and in which geography?
Does the thesis rest on a line that is a small share of revenue and of incremental growth?

inputs.funding_links: list of {id, kind: equity_stake|guarantee|take_or_pay|loan|lease_guarantee|prepayment, status: funded|committed|contingent, amount, amount_is_maximum?, direction: company_funds_customer|company_buys_from_customer|customer_funds_company, source_ids}; the same deal reported by several outlets counts once (de-duplicated by id and source)
inputs.exposed_share: {value, horizon, kind: reported|analyst_estimate, source_ids}; an analyst_estimate is attributed and never sets the level
inputs.statements: one flow window: statements {period, operating_cash_flow|cfo, net_income, non_cash_gains|non_cash_investment_gains, receivables_build|receivables_build_cash_flow_statement, related_party_revenue?, revenue?, source_ids} or the econ_fixture_v1 half_year block, else the case lines on the case period
inputs.balance: {receivables_start, receivables_end, receivables_window_months, deferred_revenue_start + deferred_revenue_window_months | deferred_revenue_start_of_year, deferred_revenue, spendable_cash|cash_and_bonds|cash_and_securities, marketable_equities (beside, never added), source_ids}
inputs.receivables_windows: earlier matched windows [{label, months, receivables_start, receivables_end, revenue_growth over the same months, source_ids}]

computes: each status as a share of annualized revenue: a stock-to-flow scale ratio, not revenue at risk
firm exposure = funded + committed (take-or-pay included); contingent kept apart and labelled ceiling
statement checks: cfo_to_ni, receivables_vs_revenue (matched windows only), receivables_build_share, customer_prepayment_build, related_party_share
funding_level
guarantee_ceiling against spendable cash
vendor_financing.boundary: ratios, never probabilities of a chain break; no default haircut; the bear mechanism funding_chain_break (WP10) needs level high and an exposed share

inputs.upstream_review_sha256: input_sha256 of the upstream econ review
inputs.share_of_revenue_via_chain: own revenue share that flows through the funded chain: a number, or {value, kind?, source_ids}
inputs.upstream: the upstream econ review, passed by the caller (econ.chain(case, upstream) / econ.review(..., upstream=)); linked by its input_sha256

computes: chain_exposure = own share x upstream exposed share, only when both exist; otherwise unquantified with the missing numbers named
upstream numbers are linked by sha256, never copied in as facts
funded_customer_chain.boundary: the link is a citation, not evidence of a dependence; a null share stays unquantified

inputs.schedule: evidenced vesting amounts per year, or null (then straight_line_assumed from the total and the term)
inputs.schedule_year: 1-based vesting year the period falls in (needed with a schedule)
inputs.observed_tranche_in_period: the tranche expensed in the period

computes: ongoing ratio = (SBC - tranche in the period) / revenue
straight-line tranche when only a total and years are given (straight_line_assumed)
tranche_schedule_mismatch when the annualized observed tranche differs from the schedule by more than rules.tranche_mismatch
the dilution is counted as real; the ratio ends when the tranche ends (WP11 sbc_pct override)
acquisition_sbc.boundary: a schedule mismatch is an open question, never resolved by assumption

inputs.segments: list of {name, revenue, prior_revenue?, profit, prior_profit?, profit_definition, model?, kpis?, source_ids}

computes: segment_reconciliation: sums against consolidated revenue and profit within rules.identity_tolerance
per-segment identity status under the segment model when one is named
segment_unexplained for any segment with at least rules.segment_material of revenue or profit and no reconciled identity
cash_cost_ratio from segment mix only when every segment has a cash-basis EBITDA (WP11); otherwise refused
segments.boundary: one consolidated margin is never applied to segments with very different margins

computes: lta_unproven (info) unless all four items are evidenced; no cycle damping without all four
WP13: +rules.coverage_extension_per_half base-reversion years per 50% covered, capped at rules.coverage_extension_cap_years; the bear never changes
contract_coverage.boundary: a tenor and a customer count alone prove nothing about price

inputs.price_to_tangible_book: P/TBV as stated (used when given; market.price / TBV is shown beside it), else market.price / TBV

computes: calls quarter._bank and extends it; never duplicates its math
excess_capital_range at both ends of the target range; never the midpoint
ROTE if all excess were returned = NI / (TCE - excess): an upper bound (the yield the excess earns is ignored)
price-implied ROTE from P/TBV = (ROTE - g) / (COE - g)
capital_lever_insufficient when even the upper bound stays below the price-implied ROTE
headroom_to_minimum
nco_basis when loan sales are disclosed and only the headline NCO is supplied
bank_capital.boundary: COE and g are explicit inputs, never defaults; no credit-loss model

text_he._doc: Hebrew vocabulary of econ.render_he (WP8): words = a plain noun phrase for every registry KPI, every growth-split and per-unit identity, and the segment items a case may mark as not disclosed; products = what the customers of a model buy (the supplier-chain sentence); note = the line under the owner's table when a text says מבני or מחזורי; boundary = the closing line of the standalone tool. Labels only: no company data, no numbers.
text_he.note: מבני = נבנה לאורך זמן ולא נעלם בשנה רעה; מחזורי = עולה ויורד עם השוק והריבית.
text_he.boundary: קריאה של המנוע העסקי; לא הערכת שווי ולא הוראת מסחר.

words.cross_buy_share: חלק הלקוחות עם יותר ממוצר אחד
words.revenue_yield_on_equity: הכנסה מכל דולר של הון לקוחות
